structuredData.name: How to survive massive crowds at Dev Deepawali festival
structuredData.description: Comprehensive safety guide for navigating 500,000+ festival attendees

step.name: Lock transport before noon
step.text: Reserve a shuttle-linked parking slot 1.5 km away (Rajghat or Dhobi Ghat) before noon to avoid barricade closures.

step.name: Arrive at ghats by 4:30 PM
step.text: Reach your chosen ghat by 4:30 PM to capture visuals before police harden barricades.

step.name: Pre-plan twin exit routes
step.text: Designate both left-bank and right-bank exit corridors so your group can pivot if one lane locks down.

step.name: Color-code your group
step.text: Use matching bands or scarves so family members can spot each other even when mobile networks fail.

step.name: Pre-download helplines and maps
step.text: Save police helpline numbers (112, 1091) and offline maps since network congestion spikes after 6 PM.

step.name: Carry a micro medical kit
step.text: Pack ORS, adhesive bandages, and dust masks to manage exhaustion and smoke-heavy segments on the ghats.

step.name: Assign buddy roles
step.text: Pair each child or elder with a dedicated adult who shepherds them through crowd surges.

step.name: Pre-book vantage points
step.text: Choose rooftop or boat access by mid-afternoon; last-minute changes can triple prices and add risk.

step.name: Capture photos early and exit before 7:45 PM
step.text: Finish key photos by 6:15 PM, then move toward pre-selected exits before the mass dispersal wave peaks.
